prerequisites: Students should have basic technical knowledge, especially a basic understanding of digital signals, simple network principles, and working with various data formats.
Basic mathematical skills, such as working with logarithms, are helpful to understand compression methods and signal processing.
For the practical part, students should be proficient in using computer and software tools and not shy away from technical hardware such as cameras, microphones, or lighting setups.
An interest in media production, a willingness to experiment, and teamwork and organizational skills also support successful work in the exercise and project phases.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a comprehensive overview of the various media types, especially audio and video, in both their analog and digital formats. This knowledge includes understanding the technical fundamentals, different signal forms, and aspects of media production.

The use of audio and video media types, especially in distributed, multimedia applications, is critically examined from a technical background. Students specialize in the technical details and theoretical foundations of data compression. They learn the principles and algorithms that lead to the reduction of file sizes of audio and video files without significant quality loss, as well as the differences between lossy and lossless compression.

The module promotes a deep understanding of the standards and formats for audio and video data. Students learn how these standards ensure compatibility between different devices and platforms and what role they play in practice, particularly in terms of quality, efficiency, and accessibility of media content.

Students work through the entire production chain of audiovisual media from creation to distribution in networks. Students can conceive and develop audiovisual applications from conception to operation, considering the technical complexity of the media types covered. The practical application of the acquired knowledge is paramount when it comes to the production and distribution of audio and video material. Students will be able to plan, implement, and evaluate their own multimedia projects. This also includes understanding and applying lighting techniques to improve the quality of productions.

Students can specify the requirements of audiovisual applications and derive the correct solution strategy for application development. They can conceive, realize, and present audiovisual media productions as a team. The ability to effectively communicate technical concepts and project ideas is another important learning objective. Students learn to work in teams, jointly develop solutions, and present their results understandably to both an expert audience and laypersons.

Students develop an awareness of the ethical, social, and cultural impacts of audio and video technology. They reflect on the responsibility associated with the creation and dissemination of media content, especially regarding copyright, data protection, and potential effects on society.

syllabus_topics: Media types Audio / Video: analog and digital signal forms
Data compression of Audio and Video

assessment_methods.method: Portfolio examination: term paper (HA) - video project of 5-8 min duration with explanation (approx. 10 minutes)

assessment_rules: The portfolio examination consists of 100 points, comprising a one-hour written exam (K1) and a term paper (HA). A maximum of 60 points can be achieved with the written exam, and a maximum of 40 points with the term paper. The experimental work (approx. 5 experiments) is an ungraded component.
